purpose: Reusable semantic backbone for explaining how institutional knowledge enables governed AI capabilities; no SEB-specific operating assertions.

nodes.label: Business work
nodes.description: A task or decision to improve.

nodes.label: Applicable authority
nodes.description: Versioned requirements and constraints; applicability must be established.

nodes.label: Domain meaning
nodes.description: Definitions and relationships, with provenance and scope.

nodes.label: Evidence and data
nodes.description: Context-specific observations and sources; availability does not imply permission.

nodes.label: AI capability
nodes.description: A bounded assistance function using permitted context and defined tools.

nodes.label: Controls and permissions
nodes.description: Policies and checks constraining information access and execution.

nodes.label: Evaluation and trace
nodes.description: Observable performance, provenance, errors and review outcomes.

edges.meaning: The task defines why assistance is useful.
Authoritative rules constrain applicable interpretation; mapping requires review.
Evidence can be used only when relevant and authorized.
Permission and risk controls govern execution.
AI assistance is not a human approval.
Observed gaps can trigger reviewed changes, never automatic policy approval.

competency_questions: What business work becomes better, faster or safer?
Which authoritative requirement applies to this case, and who validated its interpretation?
Which concept definitions and mappings does the capability use?
What evidence is available, and what is it permitted to access?
What can the AI do, and what remains a human decision?
What would reveal that the explanation or AI output is wrong?
invariants: Shared semantic meaning does not grant shared customer-data access.
A proposed mapping is not an approved requirement.
Missing evidence is unknown, not false.
AI output is not a human decision.
Operational traces may propose knowledge changes but cannot approve them.
